---
title: "Comping rhythm: Arpeggio, up and down"
subtitle: "For piano or guitar, built up a step at a time"
toc: true
toc-depth: 2
---

This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Arpeggio, up and down**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read the band's last four bars on the staff underneath. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd) · [Comping rhythms](index.qmd#chords)

## The pattern

The notes of the voicing one at a time in eighth notes, up to the top and back down, each left to ring.

It belongs in *Piano ballad*, *Jazz ballad*, *Boom-chick*, *Acoustic strum*, *12/8 doo-wop*, *Hymn (four parts)* and *Folk carol*. Here it is in the piano ballad style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="72" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Arpeggio, up and down","opts":{"compRhythm":"arp"}}]'></div>

## Step 1: Long notes

Start with something simpler. One held chord per bar (or per chord). Leaves the most room for a soloist.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords-pad.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="50" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Long notes","opts":{"compRhythm":"pad"}}]'></div>

## Step 2: Arpeggio, low and high

Eighth notes rocking between the lowest and the highest note of the voicing.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords-arp2.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="50" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Arpeggio, low and high","opts":{"compRhythm":"arp2"}}]'></div>

## Step 3: Arpeggio, up and down, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** The notes of the chord one at a time in eighths, up and back down, each left to ring. Piano: one hand position per chord, using the pedal. Guitar: hold the whole chord shape and pick string by string.

The band plays it on piano here; the step after next has it on guitar.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="50" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Arpeggio, up and down","opts":{"compRhythm":"arp"}},{"label":"Arpeggio, low and high (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"arp2"}}]'></div>

## Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 72 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's chord player off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="72" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Arpeggio, up and down","opts":{"compRhythm":"arp"}}]'></div>

## Step 5: On the guitar

The same rhythm on the guitar. On guitar each chord is a strum or a pluck of a chord shape; a short chord is choked by easing the fretting hand off the strings.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="72" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Arpeggio, up and down","opts":{"compRhythm":"arp"}}]'></div>

## Step 6: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. The pattern keeps its rhythm and changes chord where the bar does: watch the staff for the hit that lands on beat 3.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C G|Am F|Dm G|C" data-tempo="72" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Arpeggio, up and down","opts":{"compRhythm":"arp"}}]'></div>

## Step 7: In 3/4

The same pattern in a waltz: three beats to the bar. Listen for what it keeps and what it drops when the bar is a beat shorter.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="waltz" data-chart="C|C|F|F|G7|G7|C|C" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-meter="3/4" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Arpeggio, up and down","opts":{"compRhythm":"arp"}}]'></div>

## In other styles
